stem: An adult client with confirmed infection has received adequate fluid resuscitation. The client now requires a vasopressor to maintain a mean arterial pressure of 65 mm Hg and has a serum lactate level of 3.1 mmol/L. Which interpretation is most accurate?

options.A: The client meets the Sepsis-3 clinical criteria for septic shock.
options.B: The client has sepsis without shock because the mean arterial pressure is being maintained at 65 mm Hg.
options.C: The findings establish hypovolemic shock because any elevated lactate after fluid administration indicates persistent volume depletion.
options.D: The findings establish cardiogenic shock because vasopressor therapy is required to maintain perfusion pressure.

rationale: A is correct. Sepsis-3 identifies adult septic shock clinically when a client with sepsis requires vasopressors to maintain a mean arterial pressure of at least 65 mm Hg and has a serum lactate level greater than 2 mmol/L after adequate fluid resuscitation. This client meets both criteria. B is incorrect because the need for vasopressor support to maintain the pressure target is itself part of the septic-shock criterion. C is incorrect because an elevated lactate is not specific for hypovolemia, and the stem states that adequate fluid resuscitation has occurred. D is incorrect because vasopressor use alone does not establish cardiogenic shock; the infection context plus the Sepsis-3 criteria support septic shock. Current 2026 Surviving Sepsis Campaign guidance continues to treat septic shock as a medical emergency and recommends an initial MAP target of 65 mm Hg for most adults receiving vasopressors.
educational_objective: Identify adult septic shock using the Sepsis-3 clinical criteria: vasopressor dependence to maintain MAP at least 65 mm Hg plus lactate greater than 2 mmol/L after adequate fluid resuscitation.
source_organization: Society of Critical Care Medicine / European Society of Intensive Care Medicine; National Library of Medicine (PubMed)
source_document_title: The Third International Consensus Definitions for Sepsis and Septic Shock (Sepsis-3); Surviving Sepsis Campaign: International Guidelines for Management of Sepsis and Septic Shock 2026
source_version_date: Sepsis-3 published 2016; current SSC adult management guideline published 2026-03-23; accessed 2026-08-17

source_claim_supported: The Sepsis-3 clinical criteria identify septic shock in adults with sepsis who require vasopressors to maintain MAP ≥65 mm Hg and have lactate >2 mmol/L after adequate fluid resuscitation; current 2026 SSC guidance retains 65 mm Hg as the initial MAP target for most adults with septic shock.

audit_findings.source_audit: Verified the exact Sepsis-3 criteria against the original consensus publications indexed by PubMed and checked currentness against the SCCM 2026 adult Surviving Sepsis Campaign guideline published March 23, 2026.
audit_findings.claim_by_claim: The stem explicitly establishes infection, adequate fluid resuscitation, vasopressor dependence at the 65-mm-Hg MAP threshold, and lactate above 2 mmol/L. These are the specific Sepsis-3 clinical criteria. The current-guideline statement is limited to the 2026 SSC initial MAP target and does not imply that lactate alone diagnoses shock.
audit_findings.choice_A: Correct. The client satisfies the Sepsis-3 septic-shock clinical criteria.
audit_findings.choice_B: Incorrect. Maintaining MAP at 65 mm Hg only because a vasopressor is required does not downgrade the condition to sepsis without shock.
audit_findings.choice_C: Incorrect. Elevated lactate is not specific to hypovolemia, and the scenario states adequate fluid resuscitation.
audit_findings.choice_D: Incorrect. Vasopressor dependence is not specific for cardiogenic shock; the infection context and Sepsis-3 criteria identify septic shock.
audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only A incorporates all stated criteria and the infection context. C and D require unsupported etiologic assumptions, while B misinterprets vasopressor-supported MAP.
audit_findings.cueing: All options are diagnostic interpretations of similar length and clinical plausibility; no answer is grammatically cued.
audit_findings.blueprint: Directly aligned with 2026 Physiological Adaptation emergency care, altered hemodynamics/tissue perfusion, and complication recognition.
